observations: Photo 0: a black portable keyboard with speaker grilles at both ends, a central LCD, a data dial right of the display, two round controls on the left panel and a pitch bend wheel left of the keys.
'YAMAHA' is readable above the LCD in photo 0.
Keyboard spans about 36 white keys, consistent with 61 keys.
A small model label at the upper right of the panel begins 'PSR-E4' but the last digits are not legible at this resolution, so the exact model is not read.
The display is off: the keyboard is not shown powered on.
Visible scuffs, dust and wear marks on the panel and around the left speaker; keys look intact in this view.
The keyboard sits stacked between other keyboards: a Roland arranger above it and a Korg keyboard below it, with plastic wrapped items in front.
Watermark 'PATCOM GLOBAL INVESTMENT' across the keys suggests a dealer's photo.

claims.evidence: Photo 0: YAMAHA logo above the display.
Photo 0 model label is legible only as 'PSR-E4'; the last digits cannot be read. The seller's description reads like text pasted from an image tool, which is not proof.
Photo 0 key count is consistent with 61 keys.
Keyboard is not shown powered on; no clip of playing.
Needs a sound clip playing every key and the speakers at volume.
Origin cannot be shown by a photo.

risks.risk: The exact model may be an older or cheaper PSR-E4 generation than the claimed PSR-E453, and the model sets the price.
risks.proof: A sharp close up of the model label on the panel and the rating plate on the underside.
risks.if_unproven: Cannot be priced on the claimed model; a lie must not raise the price.

risks.risk: Dead keys, faulty buttons or a dead unit; it is not shown switched on.
risks.proof: A clip powering it on and running a finger across all 61 keys, then pressing the panel buttons and turning the dial.
A clip playing a demo song at high volume.
A photo of the adapter plugged in and its label.

risks.risk: Photo shows a stack of keyboards in a dealer setting; the unit sold may not be the one pictured.
risks.proof: A photo of the keyboard on its own with a handwritten note bearing today's date and a code we supply.
risks.if_unproven: Quote conditional on the agent matching the unit.

proof_requests: A sharp close up of the model label on the panel and the rating plate underneath.
A clip powering it on and playing every key, buttons and dial.
A clip of a demo song at high volume.
A photo of the adapter and its label.
The keyboard alone beside a handwritten note with today's date and our code.
response.reason: The brand is Yamaha and the series reads PSR-E4, but the last digits of the model, which set the price within the series, are not legible and the seller's PSR-E453 is only a claim. One close up of the model label settles it, after which it can be priced as not working until a playing clip is sent.
